record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Which spacetimes are asymptotically velocity dominated near a singularity, under an appropriate definition of that asymptotic behavior?

evidence.quote: Determine the class of spacetinnes which are, in an appropriately defined sense, asymptotically velocity dominated near the singularity [BKL;ELS].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $(M,g)$ be a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian spacetime satisfying the Einstein equations (possibly coupled to matter) and possessing a cosmological (crushing) singularity, foliated near the singularity by spacelike hypersurfaces $\{\Sigma_t\}$ with $t \to 0^+$ a synchronous/Gaussian time so that $g = -dt^2 + g_{ij}(t,x)\,dx^i dx^j$. The associated velocity-dominated system at $x$ is obtained from the full Einstein evolution equations by dropping all terms involving spatial derivatives of the metric and matter fields, yielding for each spatial point an ODE system whose solutions are Kasner-like. A solution $(g,\Phi)$ of the Einstein–matter system is called asymptotically velocity dominated (AVD) near the singularity if there exists a solution $(g^{VD},\Phi^{VD})$ of the velocity-dominated system on $\Sigma \times (0,T]$ such that, as $t \to 0^+$, the rescaled differences $g_{ij} - g^{VD}_{ij}$, together with appropriately rescaled derivatives and matter quantities, tend to zero pointwise (or in a suitable function-space norm).

Problem. Characterize the class of spacetimes (specifying the matter content, symmetry assumptions if any, and regularity class) that are asymptotically velocity dominated near the singularity in the above sense. Equivalently, provide necessary and sufficient conditions on initial data and matter models under which the resulting maximal globally hyperbolic development exhibits AVD behavior at its past (or future) singularity, and identify the obstructions (such as oscillatory/mixmaster behavior) preventing AVD behavior for the remaining spacetimes.
artifact.status_search_result: AVD/AVTD behavior has been proved for various special classes (e.g., Gowdy spacetimes, polarized U(1)-symmetric models, certain spacetimes with stiff fluid/scalar fields, and analytic data in some symmetric settings), and recent work continues to extend these results (e.g., silent wave equations and quiescent regimes). However, a complete characterization of which spacetimes are AVD near the singularity remains open, as generic non-symmetric vacuum singularities are expected to be oscillatory (BKL/mixmaster) rather than AVD.

status_evidence.title: Numerical Approaches to Spacetime Singularities
status_evidence.snippet: AVTD behavior is known to be characteristic of some of these models, conjectured to describe others, and probably characteristic of a subclass of the rest.
status_evidence.claim: The class of spacetimes exhibiting AVTD behavior is only partially characterized.

status_evidence.title: Numerical Evidence that the Singularity in Polarized U(1) Symmetric Cosmologies on T^3 x R is Velocity Dominated
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical evidence that polarized U(1) symmetric cosmologies have velocity-dominated singularities.
status_evidence.claim: AVD established in specific symmetric subclasses, not in general.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotics of Solutions to Silent Wave Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Recent analytic results on quiescent/velocity-dominated asymptotics for symmetric hyperbolic systems near singularities.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research extends AVD results but does not yet provide a full classification.
